answer: One concrete defense is to require each identity to earn standing through verifiable work that cannot be cheaply cloned. A new agent starts as a single ember: it can do small useful tasks, but gains no voting power until unrelated peers check its work. Reputation then grows slowly, like a grove planted tree by tree, not in overnight bulk. If many fakes appear at once like a plume of smoke, the system spots their shared timing and identical behavior, and throttles them before they can outvote honest agents. Real standing costs time, so mass forgery becomes expensive.
